question:
In the figure shown, \(\overline{US}\) and \(\overline{UT}\) are line segments each of length \(2,\) and \(m\angle TUS = 60^\circ.\)

Arcs \(\overset{\large\frown}{TR}\) and \(\overset{\large\frown}{SR}\) are each one-sixth of a circle with radius \(2.\) What is the area of the region shown?

[Figure 1](figures/2017_AMC_8_Q25_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Draw the straight segments \(ST\), \(SR\), and \(TR\). They let us replace the curved boundary with triangles and then subtract the small curved pieces.

Since \(US=UT=2\) and \(\angle TUS=60^\circ\), triangle \(UST\) is equilateral, so \(ST=2\). Each given arc is one-sixth of a circle, so its central angle is \(60^\circ\). The two radii and its chord form an isosceles triangle with a \(60^\circ\) vertex angle, hence an equilateral triangle. Therefore \(SR=TR=2\), making triangle \(SRT\) equilateral as well.

The figure places \(U\) and \(R\) on opposite sides of \(ST\). Thus the straight-sided quadrilateral \(USRT\) consists of two equilateral triangles of side \(2\). An altitude of either triangle bisects its base, so its height is
\[
\sqrt{2^2-1^2}=\sqrt{3}.
\]
Each triangle consequently has area \(\tfrac12\cdot2\cdot\sqrt{3}=\sqrt{3}\), and the quadrilateral has area \(2\sqrt{3}\).

The pictured inward arcs remove two disjoint circular segments, one beside each chord \(SR\) and \(TR\). Each segment is a \(60^\circ\) sector minus the equilateral triangle formed by its radii. Its area is
\[
\frac16\pi(2^2)-\sqrt{3}
=\frac{2\pi}{3}-\sqrt{3}.
\]
Therefore the required area is
\[
2\sqrt{3}-2\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}-\sqrt{3}\right)
=\boxed{4\sqrt{3}-\frac{4\pi}{3}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
